patterns: Driver does not support the required nvenc API version
title: NVIDIA NVENC Hardware Acceleration Failure
rootCause: The NVIDIA NVENC hardware encoder failed to initialize or crashed during transcoding.
explanation: FFmpeg attempted to initialize NVIDIA hardware video encoding, but the GPU driver either crashed, lacks supported CUDA/NVENC API capabilities, or was rejected by the system driver runtime.
recommendations: Update NVIDIA display and CUDA drivers on the host server to the latest production branch.
If running inside a Docker/LXC container, verify NVIDIA container toolkit pass-through (`--gpus all` or `/dev/dri`, `/dev/nvidia*`).
Temporarily toggle hardware acceleration to 'Advanced' or fallback to Software (libx264) in Emby Server Dashboard -> Transcoding.
Check `nvidia-smi` to ensure the GPU is not out of memory or locked by another process.

title: Intel QuickSync / VAAPI Driver Error
rootCause: Intel Quick Sync Video (QSV) or Linux VAAPI hardware acceleration failed to open the render node.
explanation: FFmpeg could not access `/dev/dri/renderD128` or communicate with the Intel media driver. Emby was forced to abort or fall back to software transcoding.
recommendations: Ensure the Emby user has access permissions to the video group: `sudo usermod -aG render,video emby`.
Install latest `intel-media-va-driver-non-free` (or equivalent QSV packages on your distribution).
Verify hardware transcoding device path in Emby Transcoding settings.

patterns: There is not enough space on the disk
title: Transcoding Storage Full / No Disk Space
rootCause: The Emby transcoding temporary cache partition has run out of available storage capacity.
explanation: During video transcoding, FFmpeg writes continuous HLS segments (`.ts` or `.m4s`) into the cache path. The partition reached 100% disk usage, causing FFmpeg write operations to abort abruptly.
recommendations: Free disk space on the partition hosting Emby's transcode directory.
Change the transcoding temporary path in Emby Dashboard -> Transcoding to a drive with larger capacity or a high-speed SSD.
Configure Emby's 'Transcoding temporary path' retention or clean up stale temp folders.

title: File System Permission Denied
rootCause: Emby or the spawned FFmpeg worker lacks read permissions for the media file or write permissions for the transcode cache directory.
explanation: The operating system rejected file system access. Either the media library storage permissions prevent the Emby service user from reading media chunks, or the transcode cache folder is read-only.
recommendations: Verify file ownership and POSIX/ACL permissions on the media and transcoding folders (e.g. `chown -R emby:emby /var/lib/emby/transcoding-temp`).
On Windows, ensure the user account running the Emby Server service has Full Control on the transcode cache directory.

patterns: An existing connection was forcibly closed by the remote host
title: Client Disconnected / Network Connection Dropped
rootCause: The remote media playback client closed the connection or experienced network interruption.
explanation: The playback stream was severed from the client end. This commonly happens when a user pauses and exits the app, closes the browser tab, experiences Wi-Fi packet dropouts, or an intermediate reverse proxy (e.g., Nginx, Cloudflare) times out.
recommendations: Check if the user intentionally stopped playback.
Inspect client Wi-Fi/cellular connection stability.
If behind Nginx or Cloudflare, ensure proxy timeouts (`proxy_read_timeout`, `proxy_send_timeout`) are set high enough (e.g. 600s) and buffering is disabled for streaming endpoints.

patterns: Invalid data found when processing input
Error splitting the input into NAL units
title: Corrupt Container or Damaged Media Bitstream
rootCause: The source media file contains corrupted headers or invalid video/audio bitstream data.
explanation: FFmpeg encountered an unrecoverable bitstream error while demuxing the media container (MKV/MP4). The file may have been downloaded incompletely or suffered storage sector corruption.
recommendations: Re-mux or re-encode the file using MKVToolNix or Handbrake.
Verify the integrity of the file: `ffmpeg -v error -i "filename.mkv" -f null -`.
Check the source storage drive for bad sectors or bit rot.

title: Subtitle Burn-In / Filtergraph Failure
rootCause: FFmpeg failed while rendering or burning graphical (PGS) or complex ASS/SSA subtitles into the video stream.
explanation: Rendering complex subtitles requires font rasterization via libass/fontconfig. Missing system fonts or malformed subtitle streams caused FFmpeg filter initialization to fail.
recommendations: Switch subtitle playback to text format (SRT) or extract subtitles externally.
Enable 'Allow subtitle extraction on the fly' in Emby Server.
Install required fonts (`fonts-dejavu-core`, `fontconfig`) on Linux hosts.

patterns: Specified pixel format .* is not supported
title: Unsupported Codec or Pixel Format
rootCause: The media utilizes an audio or video codec or pixel format unsupported by the active FFmpeg build.
explanation: FFmpeg cannot locate a compatible decoder or encoder for this stream.
recommendations: Update Emby Server to ensure the bundled FFmpeg binary includes modern codec libraries.
Convert the source file to standard H.264/H.265 with AAC audio.

patterns: Too many packets buffered for output stream
title: FFmpeg Packet Buffer Overflow / Demux Desynchronization
rootCause: FFmpeg packet buffer exceeded queue limits during muxing/transcoding (often caused by subtitle stream timestamp desync or high muxdelay).
explanation: FFmpeg buffers packets when interleaving video, audio, and subtitle streams (e.g. VTT / PGS). If one stream lags significantly behind or possesses invalid PTS timestamps, the internal packet queue fills up and triggers 'Too many packets buffered for output stream', terminating transcoding.
recommendations: In Emby Server Transcoding settings, disable 'Allow subtitle extraction on the fly' or switch subtitle track from PGS/VobSub to external SRT.
Re-mux the media container with MKVToolNix to fix subtitle stream PTS timestamp desynchronization.
Increase `-max_muxing_queue_size` if using custom FFmpeg arguments.

patterns: Session .* timed out due to inactivity
title: Playback Session Inactivity Timeout
rootCause: The playback session was terminated by Emby because no keep-alive or progress pings were received from the client.
explanation: Emby automatically reaps inactive sessions when clients suspend playback or sleep without actively notifying the server.
recommendations: This is expected normal behavior if the user paused media and walked away.
